<reason>B wins by separating protection against exclusion from an entitlement to geographic priority. Its proposed affordability allocations and buyer protections can operate before general sale, undermining A’s repeated portrayal of alternatives as competition for leftovers. B also directly challenges why hosting burdens warrant ticket privileges rather than targeted remedies, and exposes A’s narrowing of the membership alternative. A’s civic-standing argument has intuitive force, but its later speeches largely reassert that entitlement without resolving outsiders’ exclusion or the reserve’s uncertain benefit to ordinary residents.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s clarification that need-based tickets can be allocated before general sale defeats A’s central sequencing objection. A continues claiming those remedies arrive after tickets vanish, leaving B’s alternative substantially unanswered.</best_rebuttal>
